main_body: Small iron anvil: a wide face with a horn on the left, a tapering waist, and a base with a light strip, with a glowing orange piece on top.
top_band: Light steel at rows 5-6 (#d0d8e0 then #a3acb5), a 2-row band that fades into the waist below it. There is no separate top surface above a front face.
evidence: The anvil is drawn as a side profile, with horn, waist and foot in silhouette. The only light surface is a 1-2 row strip at the face (rows 5-6 at x=7), which reads as a rim. The tone grades smoothly L=215, 170, 126, 82, 61 with no step or front-edge line into a face, so it is the same family as the body. The base shows only a 1-row light strip at row 12, which is too thin to read as a surface. No horizontal surface is visible from above, so this matches the red side-elevation and rim-only examples in the guide.

style.evidence: The measured facts show 10 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references. Every dark edge pixel is neutral (100% near-neutral, #22282e), so the outline is a uniform near-black sticker line, unlike the tinted outlines of the references. The steel has a gradient of about 5 steps but no texture, grain or per-pixel variation. The piece is smaller than one tile, so it has no per-tile median. It is thinner and flatter than the stall and well references.
